Meta.title: Advantage and Yamato Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu · North Burnaby
Meta.description: Beginner-friendly No-Gi Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu in North Burnaby, BC. First class free. Black-belt instruction in English with Japanese support. Mondays & Wednesdays 8:30 PM on Hastings St, Burnaby.
Meta.ogTitle: Advantage and Yamato Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu · North Burnaby
Meta.ogDesc: Beginner-friendly No-Gi Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu. Your first class is free. English with Japanese support.

Hero.lead: A beginner-friendly No-Gi Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu academy in North Burnaby. No experience, no gi, no pressure — just safe, friendly training led by a black belt. English with Japanese support.

About.h2: run by the person who teaches it.
About.p1: Yamato is the ancient name for Japan — and the spirit this academy is built on. This isn't a franchise, but a friendly, focused No-Gi Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu class with regular members already on the mat, led by the instructor who trains right alongside you.
About.p2: Whether you want fitness, self-defense, or simply to try something new, you'll learn step-by-step in a safe, welcoming environment. Complete beginners aren't just allowed — they're who this is built for.

Train.sub: No experience needed. Every class builds the fundamentals that keep you safe and help you improve.

items.d: The foundational movements that make every technique actually work.
Clear, beginner-friendly techniques you can use from your very first day.
Controlled, cooperative drilling so you learn without getting hurt.
The why behind the how — the concepts that tie everything together.
How to train safely, with control and respect for your partner.
When you're ready, put it together with friendly, controlled live training.

Who.h1: If any of these sound like you,
items: Looking for a new way to stay fit
Want a friendly martial arts community

Philosophy.tr: Technique and timing — not strength or size — are the heart of jiu-jitsu. That principle is exactly how we teach: patient, precise, and open to everyone.

Schedule.sub: Regular members already train here, so the mat is busier than any RSVP list suggests. More class times are being added — message us for the full schedule.
Schedule.name: No-Gi · Beginner-Friendly
Schedule.moreT: Additional No-Gi classes are being scheduled. Follow on Instagram for updates.
Schedule.note: Bring comfortable athletic clothes (rashguard, tee, shorts, or leggings). No gi required.

FirstDay.sub: Walking into a martial arts gym for the first time is the hardest part. So there are no surprises — this is your first hour, start to finish.
FirstDay.note: The first class is free — including the one where you only watch.

steps.d: No paperwork, no sales pitch. Come in athletic clothes, find Hiroki, and say hi. That's the whole check-in.
Light movement to get your body ready. Go at your own pace — nobody is watching or judging you.
Hiroki demonstrates slowly, then you practice with a partner who already knows the drill. Questions are welcome.
Live training happens at the end. On day one you're free to sit it out and watch — most beginners do, and that's completely normal.
Class ends with a bow. Stay a few minutes to ask about anything — technique, schedules, or whether this is right for you.
No one will chase you for a signup. Take your time, and come back when you're ready.

Pricing.sub: Your first class is always free. No sign-up fee, no long contract.
Pricing.studentNote: Student pricing requires a valid student ID.

items: No gi required — just athletic wear
Any single class after your trial

Pricing.plSub: One-on-one coaching, tailored entirely to your goals.

Instructor.name: Hiroki Takaya
Instructor.p1: A Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu black belt from Kanagawa, Japan — where he first stepped onto the mats. Martial arts have been part of his life since childhood: he trained judo, kickboxing and Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu in Japan, and it was jiu-jitsu that captured him completely.
Instructor.p2: He discovered how rewarding it is to teach while still a university student in Japan, and went on to teach Japanese students for seven years — he holds a teaching credential in Japan for middle school and high school. Developing strong competitors interests him, but what drives him more is simply this: he wants as many people as possible to discover how fascinating Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu really is.
Instructor.alt: Hiroki Takaya — Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu black belt

items.q: I'm not fit at all. Is that a problem?
items.a: Not at all — most people start jiu-jitsu to get in shape, not the other way around. You set your own pace, and you can rest whenever you need to.
Safety is the first thing taught here. Beginners drill with control and cooperation, never competitively. You are always allowed to stop, and tapping early is respected, not judged.

items.q: Do I need a gi or any gear?
items.a: No. This is a No-Gi class — just wear a rashguard or t-shirt and shorts or leggings. Bring water and a towel.

items.q: I'm not young anymore. Am I too old?
items.a: No. Adults start jiu-jitsu in their 30s, 40s and 50s all the time. Technique and timing matter far more than youth or athleticism.

items.q: Do I need to bring a partner?
items.a: Come alone. Regular members train here every class and will happily partner with you — being the new person is how everyone started.

items.q: My English isn't strong. Is that okay?
items.a: Completely fine. Class is taught in English, and Hiroki is a native Japanese speaker — ask him anything in Japanese, any time.

Contact.sub: Your first class is free. Drop in, watch, or step on the mat — no pressure.
Contact.badgeP: Our mats are inside a full fitness facility on Hastings St, with change rooms, showers and parking. You train jiu-jitsu in a proper gym, not a back room.
Contact.bringNote: Please remove watches, rings, and necklaces, and avoid clothing with zippers or metal parts.
